figures.alt: Two maps of a forest park: in 1990 with forest, a lake, a footpath and a ranger's hut, and today with a visitor centre, café, campsite, cycle trail, boat hire and a larger car park.

features: A main road along the north edge, with a small car park
Forest covering most of the park, on both sides of the lake

A stream flowing south out of the lake

A cycle trail runs around the lake; the footpath remains

tasks.title: How paper is recycled
tasks.prompt: The diagram shows the stages in recycling used paper into new paper.

figures.alt: A nine-stage process: used paper is collected, sorted, pulped, cleaned, de-inked, drained, pressed, dried and rolled into reels of new paper.

stages.text: Used paper is collected from homes and offices.
It is sorted by type (newspaper, cardboard, office paper).
The paper is shredded and mixed with water to make pulp.
The pulp is screened to remove plastic, glue and staples.
Ink is removed with soap and air bubbles (de-inking).
The clean pulp is spread on a moving mesh so the water drains away.
Rollers press the wet sheet to squeeze out more water.
The new paper is wound onto large reels, ready to be made into products.
